title: Social stratification
examples: What is the difference between social class and social status?
Can someone really move up the social ladder?
How does the economy affect social mobility?

explain.say: Today we are learning about social stratification systems. Say what social stratification means in your own words.
Social stratification means society is arranged in layers. Say these layers are not equal in value. Say some layers have more power than others.
One way to measure this is through social class. Say class relates to wealth, income, and occupation. Say it affects your lifestyle greatly.
Next we look at social mobility. Say this refers to movement between social layers. Say you can move up or down these layers.
There are two types of mobility. Say upward mobility means moving to a higher class. Say downward mobility means moving to a lower class.
In everyday life, think about a student studying hard. Say they move from a lower-income background to a university degree. Say this is an example of upward mobility.

draw.text: Example: Education leading to higher status

faq.q: What is the main difference between social class and social status?
faq.a: Social class relates to economic factors like wealth and job. Social status relates more to prestige or reputation in society. It is common to have high status but low class.

faq.q: Is social mobility possible in every country?
faq.a: No, some societies have very rigid structures. Some countries have laws or traditions that make movement very difficult. This is often called a caste system.
asks: Are there any places where you cannot move?

faq.q: What is the role of education in social mobility?
faq.a: Education is often seen as the main way to achieve upward mobility. Say good schooling can give you the skills for better jobs. However, access to good schools can also be unequal.
asks: Does going to university guarantee success?
Is education the only way up?

faq.q: What makes a social structure rigid?
faq.a: A rigid structure means that your birth largely determines your life chances. Say the system has few opportunities for change. This is often linked to inherited status.
asks: Does where I am born decide my life?

faq.q: Can a person experience downward mobility?
faq.a: Yes, this happens due to job loss, illness, or economic downturns. Say it means falling to a lower social layer than before. This is a difficult process for many people.
asks: What causes people to fall down the ladder?

facts: Social stratification is the way societies rank people into layers.
Class is often determined by income, wealth, and occupation.
Upward mobility means moving to a higher social layer.
Ascribed status is a status you are born into.

quiz.say: A person whose family were farmers but who now works as a software engineer is showing:
quiz.why: This shows movement to a higher economic and occupational class.

wrong.0: Stasis means no change, but this scenario clearly shows change.
wrong.2: This would mean moving to a lower status than farming.
wrong.3: This describes status given at birth, not achieved later.

quiz.say: If a society believes your job role is fixed by your birth, it has:
quiz.why: Rigid structures limit movement based on birthright.

wrong.0: A meritocracy values talent over birth, making it flexible.
wrong.1: This describes changing jobs at the same level, not the core issue of rigidity.
wrong.3: High mobility means movement is easy, which is the opposite of rigid.

quiz.say: Which term describes the economic ranking based on assets and income?
quiz.why: Social class is fundamentally tied to economic standing.

wrong.0: This describes how the status was given, not the ranking system itself.
wrong.1: This is the movement between classes, not the classification system.
wrong.3: Status is more about prestige or honour, not just money.
